Thanks again for taking the call today ����— really useful conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Recap:
- Acme is focused on predictable inference latency and minimizing user-visible errors during peak traffic.
- Main competitors you're evaluating are hyperscaler managed endpoints (AWS SageMaker/Elastic Inference, GCP Vertex) and one other inference provider.
- Key questions: uptime SLA, rate limit behavior under bursts, error budget handling and failover across regions.

Proposed PoC tests (we can run these against our hosted API or Dedicated POC environment):
1) Uptime/availability: 72-hour run with synthetic traffic and periodic node failures to validate continuity and retries.
2) Rate-limit spike: ramp to 4x expected peak to observe throttling behavior and queue/backpressure.
3) Error-budget measurement: inject transient error rates and verify alerting/rollback behavior.
4) Regional failover: simulate zone outage and measure end-to-end failover time and any cold-start impact.

I've attached a short SLO comparison table and a proposed mutual action plan with suggested milestones. Can you confirm who from Acme should be on the PoC (engineering + infra)? Once we have names/dates we'll schedule the Dedicated trial and give you an endpoint and runbook.

Hi Alice �— great questions. Quick answers below, and Marissa / Aditya are copied for any deep technical follow-ups.

Q1 ��— SLA: hosted API (self-serve) typically advertises 99.9% availability for public tenants. For enterprise customers on Dedicated we offer contract SLA tiers �— common is 99.95% with penalties/credits available. For Private (VPC/on-prem) we provide an operational runbook and support SLAs tied to the support contract; uptime depends on the customer's infra and our agreed monitoring.

Q2 ��— Rate limits: we support multi-level limits. Default per-API-key limits exist, but we can configure per-route and per-tenant limits in the Dedicated control plane. For the PoC we'll surface per-tenant metrics and set custom burst windows so you can simulate tenant-level spikes without affecting others.

Q3 ��— Error budgets: our platform computes error budgets per-route and also offers an aggregated account-level view. Alerts can be emitted on either basis; most customers use route-level budgets for immediate circuit-breaking and account-level budgets for billing/operational thresholds.

Q4 ��— Failover: for hosted customers we have multi-region endpoints and active routing policies with automated fallback; typical failover time (route re-propagation + cold-start impact) is under 30s for warm pools and 60-120s worst-case for cold starts. Dedicated deployments can be configured for active-active across regions �— we recommend dedicated cross-region pools for the most predictable RTO. Private customers can implement routing per their network topology.

How this differs vs hyperscalers (short):
- Hyperscalers: often provide general purpose managed endpoints but without inference-optimized failover semantics (cold-starts can be larger; multi-region active-active requires significant infra config). Rate limiting tends to be per-endpoint/customer with less flexible per-route policies.
- Redwood: inference-first runtime with smart batching/KV cache keeps tail latencies lower during high throughput, and our control plane exposes per-route error budgets and canary rollouts + automatic fallback to smaller model variants to preserve availability.

Attachments: SLO_comparison_table.pdf (high-level matrix), Mutual_Action_Plan_ACME.xlsx (proposed milestones + owners).

Proposed PoC plan (short timeline):
- Mar 30: Kickoff + test harness access
- Mar 31 - Apr 2: Run PoC scenarios (uptime run + rate spike + failover)
- Apr 3: Review results + next steps (Dedicated trial or config changes)

If that works, I'll ask Marissa to own the test harness and provide the step-by-step scripts. Who should she coordinate with at Acme (email + preferred Slack)?

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Alice �— Marissa from Solutions Engineering here. Will own the PoC harness and test automation. A few technical notes and recommended test specifics so your SREs know what to expect: 

- KV cache & failover: our KV cache is warm per GPU pool and we persist small working sets to keep cold starts minimal. In active-active setups we replicate cache state asynchronously; expect a brief tail increase during the failover window but not full cold-start penalties if pools are warmed.
- Rate-limit test: we'll run tenant-isolated bursts using our per-route throttler and measure 95/99/99.9 latency percentiles plus server-side queue depth. We'll also demonstrate how the control plane adjusts burst windows without redeploys.
- Error injection: we can introduce transient 5xx at the model-serving layer to observe circuit-breaker behavior and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant to preserve throughput while degrading quality gracefully.
- Observability: we'll provide dashboard links (SLOs, per-route error budgets, token-level cost) and a short runbook for your on-call to watch for alerts.

Please confirm the SRE point of contact and a Slack channel (or we can use email). Once we have names I'll send the harness access and the test scripts (k6 + curl examples).

Thanks — looking forward to it.
